event_timing_assessment: (a) Source. All take 5 failures come from authored width x measured clause length, plus the first-word time for the hook. (b) The four edited events, checked against expected clause lengths. s1-event-1, width 0.11: n1 grows by two beats to about 7.0 to 7.6 s, so the payoff ends at about 1.35 to 1.42 s if the first word stays at 0.58. The limit holds while n1 is at most 8.36 s. It fails if the first word slips past about 0.66 s, so the mix --vo-at offset must keep the lead-in at take 5's level or lower. s3-event-2 and s3-event-3, width 0.17 each: n3 grows to about 6.0 to 6.5 s, giving about 1.02 to 1.11 s. The limit holds while n3 is at most 7.06 s. s7-event-1, width 0.13: n7 grows to about 8.0 to 9.0 s, giving about 1.04 to 1.17 s. The limit holds while n7 is at most 9.23 s. All four pass, and two have real margin. (c) Events the edit missed. The beats lengthen n1, n2, n3, n5, n6 and n7, and several unedited widths hit 1.2 s at small growth. s3-event-1 (width 0.2000) reaches 1.2 s once n3 passes 6.00 s, which is only +0.06 s, and the new beat after water almost certainly adds more. s6-event-1 and s6-event-2 (widths 0.1846 and 0.1847) reach it once n6 passes 6.50 s, only +0.26 s, against two new beats. Both are near-certain failures. s1-event-2 and s1-event-3 (0.1667) reach it once n1 passes 7.20 s, +0.72 s against two beats, which is likely. s7-event-2 (0.1449) reaches it once n7 passes 8.28 s, +0.64 s against two new beats, which is likely. s2-event-3 (0.2034) reaches it once n2 passes 5.90 s, +0.54 s against one beat, which is possible. s4, s5, s8, s9, s6-event-3 and s7-event-3 keep margin. (d) Will a new take re-measure all of these? Yes. board_retime recomputes every event from the new clause lengths, so the edited fractions are only as good as the length assumption behind them. The board edit is needed independently of the voice, and it has to cover every event whose width x the expected maximum clause length exceeds about 1.1 s, not only the four that failed on take 5. As a rough ceiling, with each beat up to about 0.5 s plus a few percent of pace variance, keep widths at about 0.158 or less for n1, 0.20 for n2, 0.185 for n3, 0.162 for n6 and 0.133 for n7, or split the events. Let the gate's own arithmetic confirm these figures. Fraction edits don't change the synthesized audio, so finalizing them from the measured take under the same consolidated plan would also work, if the controller allows it. (e) Runtime. Net added silence is about 2 s if the beats come out near 0.25 s and about 5 s near 0.5 s, so speech would end at roughly 56.6 to 59.6 s, before pace variance. 58.7 covers only the lower part of that range. If vo_soundcheck --cut compares the take's length with the story runtime, a long-beat take fails on the last TTS call. The ending gap (max_gap_s 4.0) limits how high the runtime can go. Inferring both constraints (not verified from gate code), a runtime of about 60 s would cover nearly the whole projected range. Before spending, confirm how vo_soundcheck's duration check and the end-gap check actually work.
